newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Issing says inflation fight not over yet.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Issing says inflation fight not over yet.

text.p: Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing said on Monday relatively low German consumer prices did not mean inflation was dead just yet.
"The danger of inflation is not dead simply because current statistics testify to price stability," Issing said in the text of a speech to a seminar at the University of Glasgow.
Issing said the scope for passing on and increasing inflationary impulses may have been narrowed due to increasing international competition.
But he said inflation in the long run was "still a monetary phenomenon" and therefore a responsiblity of monetary policy.

"The fight against inflation will not have been won definitively until inflation has disappeared once and for all from the range of attractive policy options," he said in the speech, which was made available under embargo.
Issing defended Germany's low-inflation policy, saying such a policy should not be deplored but instead be seen "as being wholesome and basically desirable".
But he said the present broad consensus on the importance of stable monetary policy is no guarantee that "the pendulum will not swing back in the other direction one day".

"If government debt, which in many countries is getting out of control, cannot be contained, inflation tax as a simple and politically 'cheap' means of solving the debt problems might once again be considered," Issing said.
